en: Cows, goats, sheep, camels, even reindeer and yaks.
People milk all kinds of animals.
So why does almost nobody drink pig milk?
Is it gross, is it dangerous, or something else? Take a guess.
I'm Max, and this is Max Wise.
Let's crack the pig milk mystery.
Some people whisper that pig milk will make you sick.
But there's no good evidence for that.
It's simply milk, made to grow piglets.
And taste isn't the deal breaker either.
The real problem is getting the milk out of the pig.
Thousands of years ago, early farmers kept cows, sheep, goats and pigs side by side.
But only some of them became dairy animals.
Start with the body.
A cow keeps her milk in one big udder with four large teats.
A farmer can milk her for several minutes at a time.
A mother pig, called a sow, is built differently.
She has two long rows of small teats, and no big udder full of milk waiting inside.
When she finally lets her milk down, it flows for only about twenty seconds.
Then it stops.
Her piglets have to wait about fifty minutes for the next round.
And there isn't much of it.
At her peak, a sow makes about twenty two pounds of milk a day, and her whole litter needs it.
An average American dairy cow makes about sixty six pounds, every single day.
Plus, a nursing sow guards her babies.
Crouching under a big, grumpy mother pig is a great way to get bitten.
So pig milk isn't poison.
Tiny teats, twenty second bursts and very little milk made pigs a terrible dairy animal.
Cows simply got the job.
Stay curious!
